name: Gorilla Biscuits
label: Revelation
lede: Queens kids named after a slang word for quaaludes made the most joyful straight edge record ever pressed, and it turned into the best-selling thing Revelation has ever put out.

eras.title: A joke name out of Queens
eras.text: Three friends from the same Queens high school started a band with a name they figured they'd drop. Then Walter Schreifels came in with a stack of songs, and the joke name was stuck to the most tuneful band in New York hardcore.

years.h: Three Queens classmates name their band after quaaludes
years.p: [[Anthony "Civ" Civarelli|a5d69704-924b-4128-9577-e16531503890]], [[Arthur Smilios|40d4f905-3bb1-4d2e-9a9b-1d7891033094]] and Nick Drysdale name their Queens band after street slang for quaaludes, pills big enough to be called gorilla biscuits. It was meant to be temporary.

years.h: [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] takes guitar and starts writing
years.p: Already playing bass in [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], Walter Schreifels picks up guitar in Gorilla Biscuits and becomes its songwriter. [[Luke Abbey|6ab9b327-0f98-4515-907c-13078f426cc5]] settles in on drums.

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits join the New York matinee crowd
years.p: Gorilla Biscuits come up in the same all-ages New York hardcore crowd as Youth of Today, [[Side By Side|8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f]] and [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]], the circle that Revelation Records starts documenting that year.

eras.title: Seven songs and a lost tape
eras.text: The Gorilla Biscuits 7" was eleven and a half minutes of hooks, cut in one January session with Don Fury. It sold well enough that Revelation kept pressing it, which is when they discovered the master tape was gone.

years.src: Revelation Records pressing history · Wikipedia: Gorilla Biscuits (album)
years.h: Gorilla Biscuits 7" · Revelation REV 4
years.p: Seven Walter Schreifels songs recorded at Demo Demo Studios in New York, produced by Schreifels and [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]]. It runs 11:35.
years.xp:
Collectors know the first press by the 102 copies with blank white and yellow labels, stamped by hand with the band's name.

After that first run the master tape went missing. Revelation had to remix the EP for every pressing that followed, so the earliest copies are the only ones that sound exactly like the session.

years.h: [[Alex Brown|bc640ea8-3500-4100-876e-6ad2b33b0390]] joins as Gorilla Biscuits' second guitarist
years.p: Alex Brown fills out the sound in time for Start Today. He already had a foot in the scene's print side: he co-created the Schism fanzine and label, which put out [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]]'s first record.

years.h: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988
yt: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988

eras.title: Start Today
eras.text: Recorded over four months and released on Revelation, Start Today took the youth crew template and made it sing. It became the label's biggest seller and the record most people mean when they talk about the sound of late-'80s New York straight edge.

years.cap: Start Today, Revelation 1989. The first pressing came in an embossed cover
years.src: Revelation Records pressing history · Wikipedia: Start Today
years.h: Start Today: fourteen songs, twenty-four minutes
years.p: Produced by Gorilla Biscuits and Don Fury at Demo² Studios, January to April. Every song is Walter Schreifels' except one [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] cover; New Direction opens it.
years.xp:
The first pressing came in an embossed cover. The seal on the shrink wrap ran top to bottom on the purple vinyl copies and left to right on the black ones, the kind of detail Rev's own pressing notes still track.

It went on to pass 100,000 CD copies, Revelation's best seller, and NME later put it among the fifteen best hardcore albums ever made.

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits aim Degradation at Nazi skinheads
years.p: Nazi skinheads were turning up at shows, some throwing salutes, and Gorilla Biscuits answered by playing Degradation, their anti-racist song, straight at them. Anthony "Civ" Civarelli later said preaching unity meant putting yourself on the line.

eras.title: Everybody's in two bands
eras.text: The Revelation circle was small, and by 1990 the same handful of players was powering half its roster. Gorilla Biscuits toured on borrowed friends, then quietly came apart as Schreifels and Civ followed new ideas.

years.h: [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] replaces Luke Abbey on drums
years.p: Youth of Today drummer Sammy Siegler replaces Luke Abbey. On the 1990 European tour Youth of Today guitarist Porcell comes along too, so it's close to a Youth of Today reunion with Civ singing.

years.h: Walter Schreifels starts [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]]
years.p: Heavier, slower and aimed somewhere past hardcore, Quicksand soon takes most of Schreifels' time away from Gorilla Biscuits.

years.h: The Gorilla Biscuits 7" comes back on CD, twelve songs long
years.p: Revelation's CD of the 1988 EP adds a Buzzcocks cover, two new originals and demo versions, stretching seven songs to nearly twenty minutes.

years.h: "Hold Your Ground" and "Start Today" live in NYC, 1991
yt: "Hold Your Ground" and "Start Today" live in NYC, 1991

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits break up
years.p: No farewell record. Anthony "Civ" Civarelli goes on to front [[CIV|1649c891-eea0-45b2-8caf-c85d985ff3bd]], a band built largely from Gorilla Biscuits players, and later opens a tattoo studio on Long Island.

eras.title: Back at the matinee
eras.text: The reunions began as favors to their own scene: a benefit at CBGB, then a return to the room before it closed for good. Over the next decade Gorilla Biscuits became one of hardcore's most dependable reunion draws, on both sides of the Atlantic.

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits reunite at CBGB for Raybeez
years.p: Gorilla Biscuits play one show, a benefit for the family of [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]] singer Raybeez, who died of pneumonia that September, as MTV reported. Alex Brown is back on guitar.

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits back at CBGB, and this time it sticks
years.p: The reunion that lasts starts at the Bowery club a year before CBGB shut its doors.

years.h: At the Matinee: twenty copies a night
years.p: Gorilla Biscuits self-release At the Matinee, with two new songs, sold only at shows, twenty copies per tour stop.

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits tour Europe again
years.p: Their first European tour since the 1990 run with Sammy Siegler and Porcell.

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits headline Webster Hall
years.p: A Manhattan headliner at the old East Village ballroom.

years.h: Gorilla Biscuits play Revelation's 25th in Pomona
years.p: Part of Revelation Records' three-night anniversary run in Pomona, California.

years.h: Start Today at 25
years.p: Revelation opens preorders for a silver anniversary pressing of Start Today, and brings back the band's Jungle T-shirt design.

eras.title: A speech and a loss
eras.text: The band that sang about unity got pulled into a fight over what unity means in 2016. Three years later it lost guitarist Alex Brown, a member since 1988.

q: My name is attached to trigger phrases that never left my mouth.
years.h: Civ's speech before Degradation at This Is Hardcore
years.p: At This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia, Anthony "Civ" Civarelli introduces the anti-racist song by saying people shouldn't still need Black Lives Matter shirts, and that everyone matters. Critics hear an All Lives Matter line.
years.xp:
The backlash was quick and loud across punk media. Civ's side: he meant that a basic truth shouldn't need a slogan on a shirt, and he pointed to decades of songs about unity and against judging people.

His critics' side: at that moment, recasting Black Lives Matter as everybody matters was exactly the move the movement was pushing back against. The argument never fully resolved.

years.src: NME · Spin · Brooklyn Vegan · Mainframe Studios
years.h: Guitarist Alex Brown dies at 52
years.p: Early reports said aneurysm; Anthony "Civ" Civarelli corrected it on Instagram: Alex Brown died of natural causes, a basal ganglia stroke. [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]], Civ's guitarist in CIV, takes his place in Gorilla Biscuits.
years.xp:
By then Brown was a painter who had shown in New York, Tokyo, Geneva and Brussels. Born in Des Moines in 1966, he studied at Parsons. His paintings took found photos from travel brochures and postcards and laid gridlike patterns over them by hand, work that Brooklyn Vegan and others noted in their obituaries. He also designed sleeves for [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]].

Civ called him a friend of over thirty years. Arthur Smilios put it in stage terms: stage right was going to feel it.
